sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Wayne County
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Recorder of Deeds in the Wayne County Courthouse Annex, 925 Court Street, Honesdale, PA 18431. Call 570-253-5970, extension 4040. The doors are open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and nothing is taken for recording after 4:00 p.m.

This office is the custodian of land transfer records and indexes. It holds deeds, mortgages, subdivision plans, rights-of-way and easements, and it also files the commissions and oaths of county officials, district justices and notaries, plus military discharges. For a house sale, the last step happens in Honesdale: after closing, the signed deed is filed and the buyer appears as owner of record.

Legal advice and attorney referrals are not something the staff provide. For help wording a deed, hire a lawyer. The Wayne County Bar Association keeps a member list.

UPI certification started on November 2, 2026, at $20.00 per UPI number. A deed for a parcel now includes this certification step, and a sale covering more than one parcel pays the $20.00 once for each UPI number.

The recorder's page links a UPI notice. Ask for it, and have your closing agent or attorney confirm when the certification must be finished so it does not hold up the filing.

The same date changed another number: the deed recording fee for a tax sale deed became $94.75. That figure applies to tax sale deeds, so ask the office what an ordinary private sale deed costs.

Wayne County posts a fee schedule as a spreadsheet and a PDF, listed by document type. These are the amounts that appear on its recorder and tax sale pages.

Wayne County recorder and tax sale charges

For the total on an ordinary deed, call 570-253-5970, extension 4040, or open the fee schedule on the Recorder of Deeds page.

Two vendors handle electronic filing: CSC at 866-652-0111 and Simplifile at 800-460-5657. Most land documents can go this way, which saves a trip to Honesdale.

Two kinds of document must be delivered on paper: subdivision plans, and deeds that are taxable in more than one jurisdiction. The second exception applies when a parcel lies in more than one municipality. The deed then has to state the percentage in each so the local transfer tax divides correctly.

  • E-recorded transactions with a REV-183 Statement of Value attach helper pages at $0.50 each.
  • Paper filings must reach the courthouse annex before 4:00 p.m.
  • Faxed or emailed copies are not accepted for recording.

sections.h2: What the recorder requires on a deed
sections.html:
The recorder's checklist is stricter than many sellers expect. An acknowledgment must show the county, state, date, the people or corporate officers appearing, and the notary's signature, stamp and expiration date. Miss any of those and the acknowledgment is treated as defective.

  • The written amount of consideration has to match the number on the deed.
  • Every deed, mortgage and assignment needs a signed certification of the grantee's address with zip code.
  • Transfer taxes or a completed Statement of Value must accompany every deed.
  • Use black ink on white or manila paper, since the office scans everything.
  • Documents may not exceed 8 1/2 by 14 inches, and maps may not exceed 24 by 36 inches.
  • Recorded papers come back by mail only if you enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope.

sections.h2: Wayne County housing at a glance
sections.html: Wayne is a rural Poconos county with about 51,703 residents. Owners occupy 80.5 percent of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $242,100, and median gross rent is $1,038. The county counts 32,637 housing units but only 20,877 households, so a large share of homes are not lived in year-round. That affects who your likely buyers are, and a house that heats well in winter will draw more attention at inspection.

The Assessment Office keeps property records and prepares the tax rolls. It does not set millage rates or collect taxes. You will find it at 925 Court Street in Honesdale, phone 570-253-5970, extension 4010, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Back taxes go to the Tax Claim Bureau, extension 4000, at the same address. It runs sales under the Real Estate Tax Sale Law, and unsold properties move to a repository list. Repository sales happen quarterly, in February, May, August and November, and the owner can pay up to the day of the sale. Buyers at a repository sale pay costs, a $25 deed preparation fee and 2 percent transfer tax, and Act 33 requires every bidder to pre-register.

If a back-tax balance sits on the house you want to sell, ask the Tax Claim Bureau for a payoff figure before closing so it can be paid from your proceeds.

sections.h2: From closing table to public record
sections.html:
Once you sign, the title company or attorney assembles the package: the deed, the Statement of Value or the transfer tax payment, the grantee address certification, and the fees. Check the package against the checklist above before it leaves their office, because a missing notary stamp or a mismatched dollar amount gets the filing returned.

If the deed goes in electronically, CSC or Simplifile carries it to the recorder. If it goes on paper, someone must reach the annex before 4:00 p.m. and include a stamped, self-addressed envelope if you want the original back. A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, but the recording steps and the transfer tax stay the same.

Before the day arrives, ask your closing agent three things: whether the parcel needs UPI certification and for how many numbers, whether the deed touches more than one municipality, and whether the file will go on paper or electronically. Those answers decide the fees and the route. Keep the recorded deed when it comes back, since it proves the transfer is on the public record. If the office rejects a filing, ask exactly which item failed, fix it and resubmit the same day if you can.

faqs.q: What are the Wayne County Recorder of Deeds hours?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., but it takes no documents for recording after 4:00 p.m. It is in the Courthouse Annex at 925 Court Street in Honesdale, and the phone is 570-253-5970, extension 4040.

faqs.q: Is there a new fee for parcel identifiers in Wayne County?
faqs.a: Yes. Uniform Parcel Identifier certification began on November 2, 2026, and costs $20.00 per UPI number. The recorder's page links a UPI notice that explains the process.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a Wayne County deed?
faqs.a: Yes, with exceptions. Use CSC (866-652-0111) or Simplifile (800-460-5657). Subdivision plans and deeds taxable in multiple jurisdictions cannot be e-recorded and must go in on paper.

faqs.q: Does Wayne County mail back a recorded deed?
faqs.a: Only if you enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope when you submit it.

faqs.q: Where do I see who owns a Wayne County parcel?
faqs.a: Search recorded documents on Landex, which the county uses for online records. Index searching is free, and you pay only when you buy copies of documents to download or print.
